title.rendered: Morgan's moment to shine

excerpt.rendered: Mercedes double plus a win for Cammish at Donington Park...

content.rendered:
Mercedes double plus a win for Cammish at Donington Park

Adam Morgan has enjoyed arguably the finest fortnight of his Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship career to date, with the CPRL driver claiming two wins at Donington Park this weekend (22/23 August) after taking his first victory of the season at Knockhill last time out.

Not only has the Mercedes man claimed three race victories in recent weeks, but he has also doubled his pole position tally, having topped qualifying at each of the last two events after previously taking just one pole, back in 2018.

It was also a memorable day for Dan Cammish, as the NAPA Racing UK driver took his second win of the season to strengthen his championship challenge, moving to within five points of second-placed Tom Ingram in the overall Drivers’ standings.

A strong collection of points for Ash Sutton still sees the four-time champion hold a comfortable margin at the top of the order, whilst his Alliance Racing/Ford and NAPA Racing UK outfit further extended their advantage in the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ and Teams’ tables.

The Power Maxed Racing stable continues to enjoy a stellar season with its quartet of all-new Audi A3 Saloons, as Mikey Doble leads the Independent Drivers’, Dexter Patterson tops the Jack Sears Trophy and LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing hold sway in the Independent Teams’ order.

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship continues its run towards the final stretch of the season with the next event taking place at Croft Circuit in North Yorkshire in two weeks’ time (5/6 September).

Morgan converts pole into emphatic win

Following his 'Race to Pole' triumph at the famous Leicestershire circuit on Saturday, Morgan duly converted that success into a commanding victory in the first race on Sunday.

The squabble for second arguably helped as teammate Dan Rowbottom (CPRL – Mercedes) initially lost out to Speedworks Corolla Racing's Josh Cook and then current championship leader Sutton in his #116 NAPA Racing UK Ford Focus Titanium.

The opening lap provided one of the most dramatic moments of the season so far when Lewis Gilbert's WSR BMW speared off into the barrier on the approach to the Melbourne Loop. The BMW 330i M Sport then dug into the grass before barrel rolling aggressively and coming to a halt.

A shaken Gilbert was given the all clear by the TOCA Medical Team shortly after although of course still taken to the Medical Centre for further observation, whilst the same condition couldn't be said for his stricken Bavarian machine.

Morgan led away following the restart with Cook's Toyota Corolla in a good second place, whilst Sutton and Rowbottom fought behind.

Disaster struck for Cook, however, when a throttle issue slowed his car into retirement.

Sutton defended valiantly from Rowbottom with the latter eventually relinquishing third to Gordon Shedden in his Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport Toyota. Another place was given up on the final tour when Cammish's NAPA Racing UK Ford muscled past the Mercedes for fourth.

Cammish collects second win of 2026 campaign

Among the current grid, Cammish has now claimed more victories on the famed Donington Park Grand Prix circuit than any other driver, with three wins putting him clear of title rivals Sutton and Ingram.

Coincidentally, it was the same three drivers filing the podium positions in this particular race as the trio got the better of early leader Rowbottom in his CPRL Mercedes.

Cammish made his move at the final corner shortly before mid-distance as the #27 Ford Focus Titanium brushed his way through and into the lead.

Rowbottom initially fought back before dropping into the clutches of Sutton, who was impressively keeping pace despite running minimal boost and the Goodyear hard tyre compound on his NAPA Racing UK Ford. Rowbottom then slowed exiting the chicane late on and was soon shuffled further down the order by Sutton and Ingram.

The #32 Mercedes held on to fourth from the chasing Ricky Collard (Team VERTU – Hyundai) and Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing – Audi), the latter again impressively taking Independents' and Jack Sears Trophy honours.

Mighty Morgan strikes again

CPRL's Morgan was again triumphant in the Donington Park finale, becoming only the second driver to take three victories so far this season.

Morgan’s Mercedes applied pressure to pole-sitter Chris Smiley from the start, as the Restart Racing Hyundai driver worked hard to keep those behind at bay.

Smiley’s defence didn't last long however, as Morgan blasted by and immediately set about pulling away, which he duly did with consummate ease.

When the chequered flag fell Morgan had romped clear to win from the brilliant Aiden Moffat in the LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing Audi, with the latter receiving huge applause from his PMR squad and fans.

Young Daryl De Leon completed the podium positions as he provided some respite for the WSR team. A destroyed BMW earlier in the day and mixed results for their trio of drivers had provided frustrations at the Leicestershire circuit, but De Leon produced the goods in the finale to score a richly deserved podium.

title.rendered: Adam Morgan takes third win of 2026 with commanding drive

excerpt.rendered: CPRL's Adam Morgan was triumphant in Round 21 of the...

content.rendered:
CPRL's Adam Morgan was triumphant in Round 21 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Donington Park, becoming only the second driver to take three victories this season.

Morgan's Mercedes harassed pole-sitter Chris Smiley from the off, as the Restart Racing Hyundai tried desperately to fend off those behind.

His defence didn't last long as Morgan blasted by and immediately set about pulling away, which he duly did with consummate ease.

A man in arguably the finest form of his career had already claimed pole position and a race win earlier in the weekend so there was little chance of him giving up another opportunity to reach the top step of the rostrum.

When the chequered flag fell Morgan had romped clear to win from the brilliant Aiden Moffat in the LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing Audi, with the latter receiving huge applause from his PMR squad and fans.

Young Daryl De Leon completed the podium positions as he provided some respite for the WSR team. A destroyed BMW earlier in the day and mixed results for their trio of drivers had provided frustrations at the Leicestershire circuit, but De Leon produced the goods in the finale to score a richly deserved podium.

The Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport squad completed a solid day with Árón Taylor-Smith and Gordon Shedden finishing in fourth and seventh respectively, with Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK) and Charles Rainford (WSR) wedged between them in the order.

Josh Cook (Speedworks Corolla Racing) and Tom Ingram (Team VERTU) scrapped hard over eighth, the pair briefly making contact through the chicane late in the race, but the former held on to take the place.

Dexter Patterson scored a hat-trick of top tens during the day as the Scotsman continues to turn heads in his Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing Audi.

There was another incident of note that was reviewed post-race as title rivals Sutton and Ingram clashed on-track. Championship leader Sutton was adjudged to have been in the wrong as he nudged his way past and was subsequently handed a five second penalty, changing the order in the bottom half of the top ten.

NAPA Racing UK's Dan Cammish stood victorious in Round 20 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Donington Park, moving up to second in the overall Drivers' standings in the process.

Of the current grid, Cammish now has more victories around the famed Grand Prix circuit than any other driver with three wins – pulling clear of title rivals Ash Sutton and Tom Ingram.

Coincidentally, it was the same three drivers filing the podium positions in this particular race as the trio got the better of early leader Dan Rowbottom in the CPRL Mercedes.

Cammish made his move at the final corner shortly before mid-distance as the #27 Ford Focus Titanium brushed his way through and into the lead.

Rowbottom initially fought back before he fell back into the clutches of Sutton – incredibly keeping pace while running with minimal boost available as well as the Goodyear hard tyre compound on his NAPA Racing UK Ford. Rowbottom then slowed coming out of the chicane late on and he was soon shuffled further down the order by Sutton and Ingram.

The #32 Mercedes held on to fourth from the chasing Ricky Collard (Team VERTU) and Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing), the latter again impressively taking Independents' and Jack Sears Trophy honours.

Árón Taylor-Smith (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport) and Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) were next in the order, whilst polesitter Adam Morgan (CPRL) and Chris Smiley (Restart Racing) completed the top ten.

Smiley was further rewarded post-race by scooping pole position for the reverse-grid contest later this afternoon.

The podium celebrations belonged to Cammish however, as his 18th career victory propelled him just one point ahead of Ingram in the standings, and he now becomes teammate Sutton's closest championship challenger.

title.rendered: Adam Morgan does the double!

excerpt.rendered: CPRL driver tops teammate Dan Rowbotton in Donington Park Qualifying...

content.rendered:
CPRL driver tops teammate Dan Rowbotton in Donington Park Qualifying Race

It was a Mercedes one-two in today's Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship 'Race to Pole' around the legendary Donington Park GP circuit as Adam Morgan topped CPRL teammate Dan Rowbottom.

Incredibly, Morgan has doubled his BTCC career pole positions in just two weeks, having secured P1 at Knockhill last time out. Prior to that, the Lancastrian's only qualifying top spot came at Rockingham way back in 2018.

The result highlights the incredble progress made by the pair of Mercedes A35 Saloons since the mid-summer break.

Rowbottom secured the car's first overall podium at Thruxton in July before four more followed in the trip north of the border, including Morgan's first win of the season.

Starting the Donington Park GP Qualifying Race from pole and third respectively handed the CPRL outfit another great opportunity to impress and their situation was immediately enhanced when Rowbottom nipped by front-row starter Josh Cook on the run down to Redgate.

Cook kept Rowbottom honest during a couple of restarts, but the latter fended off the #66 Speedworks Corolla Racing machine to secure the place.

Multiple race winner Cook ended up having to go quite defensive towards the finish as the always charging Ash Sutton filled his mirrors in the #116 NAPA Racing UK Ford Focus Titanium.

Sutton had to settle for fourth, but it still represented a solid improvement from seventh on the grid as he ultimately extended his championship advantage.

Just over a second separated fifth to ninth in the order as Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) kept the Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport duo of Gordon Shedden and Árón Taylor-Smith at bay, as they – like Cook – showed the pace of the Toyota Corollas at their home track.

Tom Ingram (Team VERTU – Hyundai) and Sam Osborne (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) were eighth and ninth respectively, whilst Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) continued his good form with another top ten finish.

Rounds 19, 20 and 21 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship take place at Donington Park tomorrow with the action getting underway on ITV4 at 1100.

title.rendered: Ingram tops free practice at Donington Park GP

excerpt.rendered: Tom Ingram made his pace clear in the weekend’s only...

content.rendered:
Tom Ingram made his pace clear in the weekend’s only Free Practice session as the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship descended on the Donington Park GP Circuit.

The fast and frenetic 50-minute session saw all 23 cars take to the track, completing hundreds of miles around the famous Leicestershire venue.

There was one stoppage during the single practice session as Josh Cook's Speedworks Corolla Racing's machine came to a halt after the Old Hairpin. The momentary pause saw Charles Rainford's WSR BMW lead the way, but the times came tumbling down after the green flag waved once more.

When the chequered flag fell it was Mikey Doble second behind Ingram, ahead of Dan Rowbottom (CPRL), Rainford and Knockhill race winner Adam Morgan (CPRL).

As a reminder, the finishing order of Free Practice is now split into two groups, odd-finishing-numbers (Group 1) and even-finishing-numbers (Group 2), for a 15-minute qualifying session to set their fastest times.

The group with the fastest qualifying time will occupy the odd-numbered grid positions for the Qualifying Race, ordered by their respective qualifying times. The other group will occupy the even-numbered grid positions, also ordered by qualifying times.

15 minutes after the qualifying session for Group 2 has concluded, the standard grid procedure for a race start begins, and the pit lane opens. The finishing order of the shorter nine lap ‘Race to Pole’ will determine the grid for the first of Sunday’s traditional trio of races.

Half-points are awarded for the Qualifying Race. There are no bonus points for leading a lap, the fastest lap, or for pole position for the Qualifying Race, whereas the bonus points for leading a lap and the fastest lap are still available on Sunday.

Qualifying and the Qualifying Race can be found LIVE on the ITV Sport YouTube Channel worldwide from 13:50 later today.

title.rendered: Donington Park next for WSR as Rainford reaches 50th BTCC start

excerpt.rendered: WSR continues its 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship...

content.rendered:
WSR continues its 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season at Donington Park this weekend (22/23 August) as driver Charles Rainford prepares for his 50th start in the series.

Unlike at the season-opening round in April, the upcoming event takes place on the full 2.49-mile ‘Grand Prix’ layout of the East Midlands track, with the ‘Melbourne Loop’ added to the ‘National’ circuit.

After scoring a podium finish at that season-opener, Rainford is back and looking for more aboard his BMW 330i M Sport.

The Horsham driver, who has two wins to his name in 2026 and holds fifth place in the Drivers' standings, reaches a significant career milestone this weekend as race two at Donington is set to be the 50th of his BTCC career.

Teammate Daryl De Leon enjoyed his visit to Donington’s GP circuit last year as he took a perfect score in the Jack Sears Trophy with class victories in all three races as he surged to the title at the end of the season.

That weekend included a pair of overall top-10 finishes for the Cambridgeshire-based Anglo-Filipino, who holds second place in the Independent Drivers’ standings – one point ahead of Rainford – and is aiming to close significantly on the series lead.

Lewis Gilbert, also aboard a WSR BMW, is preparing for only the third BTCC event of his career. The Scotsman, from Dalry, North Ayrshire, ran competitively in the final race at his home circuit of Knockhill recently with peak lap times almost on a par with the race winner.

This will be the 22-year-old’s first time racing at Donington Park; his rookie season in racing has encompassed mainly circuits on the European continent before he took part in the BTCC events at Thruxton and Knockhill.

Charles Rainford: “Fifty races in the BTCC! That’s come around really quickly. It only feels like yesterday that I was making my debut – also at Donington, but on the shorter circuit – and it’s amazing how things have progressed since then with a handful of wins, a pole position and more podiums. The target for this weekend is 100 per cent to add more, score as many points as I can and move up the championship table.”

Daryl De Leon: “Donington GP was a strong event for me last year as I won the Jack Sears Trophy in all three races and had a very strong performance in Race Two coming from the back to finish in the top five. Currently I’m second in the Independents’ points and if we can have a strong weekend, I’m sure I can close in on the leader and make it a really good fight for the title. We’ve had the pace recently, so I’m confident of our chances.”

Lewis Gilbert: “My first two BTCC events have been a really steep learning curve at Thruxton and Knockhill – because they’re such unique tracks – aren’t the best places to really try to click with your car. Donington is a much more conventional racetrack; it’s wide, smooth and has lots of medium-speed corners, so I think I can probably make more gains with my driving here than any other track so far. A clean weekend and some points finishes – which I think we deserved at Knockhill with the pace we had – would be really satisfying to come away with.”

title.rendered: Speedworks Corolla Racing ready to attack Donington GP circuit

excerpt.rendered: Speedworks Corolla Racing returns to familiar territory this weekend as...

content.rendered:
Speedworks Corolla Racing returns to familiar territory this weekend as the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads back to Donington Park this weekend (22/23 August) – this time taking on the Grand Prix circuit.

The Cheshire-based squad began this year's campaign at the Leicestershire venue back in April, when the championship raced on Donington’s National configuration.

On that occasion, Josh Cook immediately demonstrated the potential of the Toyota Corolla GR Sport, qualifying inside the top six before fighting right at the front in the Race to Pole.

Cook carried that momentum into Sunday and again looked capable of challenging for victory in the opening race before a puncture cruelly brought his charge to a premature end.

Four months later, Speedworks returns determined to rediscover that level of performance as the championship tackles the longer and more technically demanding Grand Prix layout.

The weekend provides an immediate opportunity to respond following a challenging visit to Knockhill last time out.

Despite Cook producing a determined recovery through the field on Sunday, the Scottish weekend ultimately fell short of the team’s expectations.

Speedworks therefore heads south with a clear objective – to attack the Donington weekend from the outset and translate the underlying potential of the Corolla into stronger qualifying and race results.

Alongside Cook, Ryan Bensley continues to build experience in his first BTCC campaign with Speedworks.

Having joined the team at Thruxton, Bensley now has two complete race weekends in the Corolla under his belt and heads to Donington increasingly comfortable with both the car and the demands of the championship.

Knockhill provided another important step forward for Bensley. Despite the final results not fully reflecting his performance, his pace relative to the field was encouraging throughout the weekend, particularly around a circuit where the entire grid was separated by exceptionally small margins.

With valuable mileage and experience now behind him, Bensley arrives at Donington highly motivated to turn that progress into another step forward.

For Speedworks Corolla Racing, the return to the venue where its season began therefore represents an opportunity to reset, respond and attack the latest chapter of an intensely competitive BTCC campaign.

Christian Dick, Team Principal, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: “Donington was a really positive place for us at the start of the season. Josh was right at the sharp end from the outset, and we showed that weekend that we had the pace to fight at the front.

“Knockhill was frustrating and ultimately wasn’t the weekend we wanted, so the best response is to get straight back out there and attack Donington.

“The Grand Prix circuit obviously presents a different challenge to the National layout, but we know the foundations of the package are strong and we’re going there determined to put ourselves back amongst the front-runners.

“Ryan is also making really good progress. Knockhill was encouraging in terms of his outright pace and, with two weekends now under his belt, he’s becoming increasingly comfortable within the team and the car. I’m looking forward to seeing what both drivers can do.”

Josh Cook, Speedworks Corolla Racing Driver, said: “I’m looking forward to getting back to Donington. The opening weekend of the season feels a long time ago now, but we had some really strong pace there and were genuinely in the fight at the front.

“We qualified well, had a really strong Race to Pole and then felt we were in contention for a big result on Sunday before the puncture, so there are definitely good memories and plenty of positives to take back with us.

“Knockhill was a tough weekend, but we kept fighting and recovered some decent results from where we started. Now we need to reset and attack Donington.”

Ryan Bensley, Speedworks Corolla Racing Driver, said: “I’ve got a couple of weekends under my belt now and I’m feeling more comfortable in the car every time I get in it.

“Knockhill was really encouraging from a pace point of view. The results perhaps didn’t show the whole picture, but I felt like we made another good step and I was much closer to where I want to be.

“That gives me a lot of confidence going into Donington. I’m understanding the Corolla better, I’m getting to know the team and how everything works over a BTCC weekend, and now I want to start turning that progress into results.

“I’ve definitely got the bit between my teeth. I’m really motivated, I can’t wait to get back in the car and I’m going to Donington determined to get stuck in and keep moving forward.”

title.rendered: Where to Watch: Donington Park GP

excerpt.rendered: The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads back...

content.rendered:
The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads back to the season's starting point at Donington Park this weekend (22/23 August) for the seventh event of the year, this time around the iconic GP layout.

After three different victors at Knockhill, the BTCC heads to the Leicestershire venue as Ash Sutton leads the way for a rampant weekend of action around the 2.49-mile circuit.

The weekend gets underway with Free Practice, then we go straight into qualifying. Two groups of 15-minute sessions, split according to the finishing order from Free Practice between odd and even finishing positions. The group with the fastest time will take the odd-numbered grid spots for the Qualifying Race. 15 minutes after qualifying, the pit lane opens ahead of the ‘Race for Pole’. A nine-lap race will then take place with half points awarded, as the result forms the grid for the first of the traditional trio of races on Sunday.

Last time out, the 2026 grid headed to Fife for the sixth race weekend of the championship. After another sensational Saturday, culminating in the all-new ‘Race to Pole’, Adam Morgan would take his maiden Qualifying Race victory, setting Sunday up for the perfect start as the Lancastrian driver then took his first victory of the season. Championship leader Sutton would stand triumphant in Race 2, with a performance that saw the four-time champ yet again extend his lead in the standings. The final race of the weekend saw Tom Chilton take his first victory of the season, becoming the 10th different winner of 2026.

This weekend’s race day action will feature on the home of the BTCC, ITV4, from 1100 on Sunday (23 August), while the ITV YouTube page will host the Qualifying Race and Qualifying on Saturday (22 August) from 1400.

As in 2025, each race day of the season – including all support series’ races – will be streamed LIVE around the globe on the BTCC YouTube channel, with the exception of the UK and North America, which have existing broadcast arrangements.

The BTCC will be aired LIVE in North America (US and Canada), continuing the multi-year agreement with the RACER Network, streaming live and on demand as part of a long-term agreement with the championship.

All 30 races are scheduled to air on the main RACER channel, whilst support series’ and extended BTCC highlights will be available to watch via the RACER+ App, the network’s premium motorsports streaming platform. Race 1 will begin at 06:45 Eastern Time (ET), with Race 2 following at 09:45 ET and Race 3 closing out the day’s racing at 12:30 ET.

title.rendered: A Statement

excerpt.rendered: Following today’s (18 August) statement from Cataclean, TOCA confirms the...

content.rendered:
Following today’s (18 August) statement from Cataclean, TOCA confirms the team will continue competing in the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship under a new name and management structure, in order that it can move positively forward.

The matters concerned are internal to the organisation and relate solely to its directors, shareholders and relevant parties. TOCA is not privy to those matters.

However, TOCA has been provided with assurances of the team’s participation in the BTCC going forward. Those assurances reflect Cataclean’s continuing commitment and confidence in both the team and the Championship.

We understand that the programme will operate through a new entity, without the further involvement of Jason Plato in its management or ownership.

In the interim, the team will be entered as CPRL.

Jason is unquestionably one of the BTCC’s greatest stars, and his exceptional record speaks for itself. He has long been – and will remain – a valued part of the BTCC family. Although his involvement with this particular venture appears to have reached its conclusion, we look forward to seeing Jason in the BTCC paddock in the future.

title.rendered: Donington Park GP awaits Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport

excerpt.rendered: Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport head to Donington Park...

content.rendered:
Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport head to Donington Park this weekend (22/23 August) for event seven of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship, returning to the venue for a second time this season, this time on the longer GP configuration.

The squad arrives on the back of a front-row start, podium finish and an Independent victory at Knockhill, where home hero Gordon Shedden claimed the 142nd rostrum of his career and team-mate Árón Taylor-Smith banked a solid points haul in Fife. The aim now is to carry that momentum back to the scene of the season opener.

At 2.49 miles, the GP layout adds a further test for the drivers and opens up more genuine overtaking opportunities, with the addition of the Melbourne Hairpin.

Both drivers have form at the extended layout. Dubliner Taylor-Smith swept to a hat-trick of Independent class wins on the GP circuit in 2024, in addition to a hard-fought overall second place in 2023. Shedden, meanwhile, has eight victories at the Leicestershire venue, with his outing on the GP circuit last year rewarding him with a third-place finish.

Heading into round seven, Shedden occupies tenth in the Drivers' Championship, with Taylor-Smith occupying 14th. Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport sit sixth in the Teams' Championship and third in the Independent Teams' Championship, with the team focused on closing the gap in both standings as the second half of the season continues.

Following Saturday morning's opening 50-minute Free Practice session (11:00), the all-important Qualifying session (14:05) and 9-lap Qualifying Race (15:05) will determine the grid for Sunday's three races.

Sunday's races are scheduled for 11:45, 14:45 and 17:30 (BST), with all three broadcast live on ITV4 and ITVX in the UK, Racer Network in North America, and the BTCC YouTube channel everywhere else in the world.

Árón Taylor-Smith (#50) said: "Donington GP is a circuit that holds plenty of good memories for me, with the likes of my return to the podium in 2023 after seven years away, and then the hat-trick of Independent wins in 2024. Knockhill was a challenging weekend for us with reliability issues, but we came away knowing we had the pace to fight at the sharp end with a bit of luck on our side. Plenty of homework has been done back at base to put us back in the mix this weekend. These races are won & lost in the workshop, and I’m confident that once the car is in the window, we can challenge once again."


Gordon Shedden (#52) said: "It's good to be heading back to Donington, and to the venue of my first podium with Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport at the start of the year. The GP circuit offers something a bit different with the hairpin thrown in, and that opens up some interesting overtaking opportunities come race day. Knockhill was a highlight for us, with a strong Saturday and a solid race day, delivering another podium and an Independents win to the tally. We had good pace all weekend, so the focus now is on taking that performance, executing properly, and coming away with another big haul of points."

title.rendered: Dan Lloyd Returns to Restart Racing for Remainder of 2026 BTCC Season

excerpt.rendered: Restart Racing has confirmed that reigning BTCC Independent Drivers’ Champion...

content.rendered:
Restart Racing has confirmed that reigning BTCC Independent Drivers’ Champion Dan Lloyd will return to the team for the remainder of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season, replacing James Dorlin from this weekend’s event at Donington Park GP (22/23 August).

The change follows confirmation that Dorlin will step away from Restart Racing after six events with the team in 2026. He joined the squad at the beginning of the campaign alongside Chris Smiley and enjoyed Jack Sears Trophy success at Brands Hatch, before producing his strongest weekend of the season at Thruxton with three top-ten finishes, two Independents’ victories and another Jack Sears Trophy win.

Lloyd will now return to the wheel of a Hyundai i30 N Fastback, reuniting with Smiley and a team he knows extremely well after playing a central role in Restart Racing’s breakthrough 2025 season. He claimed the squad’s first outright BTCC victory with a memorable win at Silverstone before going on to secure the Independent Drivers’ Championship.

Together with Smiley, Lloyd also helped Restart Racing claim the Independent Teams’ Championship, completing a landmark campaign for the squad in only its second year of BTCC competition.

Although Lloyd stepped away from competing in the championship at the end of 2025, he has remained closely involved with Restart Racing throughout this season in an advisory role on race weekends.

Pete Jones, Team Principal of Restart Racing, said: “We’re absolutely delighted to have Dan back in the car. He knows the team, he knows the car and we know exactly what he is capable of. What we achieved together last year was incredibly special, so having the reigning Independent Champion back behind the wheel feels like a great fit for us.

“Dan has remained a big part of the team this year and has been with us at race weekends in an advisory role, so he has stayed very close to what we are doing and how the car has developed.

“He also has a brilliant relationship with everyone in the team and with Chris, which means he can come straight back in and get on with the job.

“We still have a lot we want to achieve this season and there are plenty of opportunities ahead of us. Bringing Dan back gives us a proven race winner who knows how to get the very best out of this car, and I think everyone in the team is excited to see what we can do together over the remaining rounds.”

Dan Lloyd said: “First of all, I want to say that I know this is a difficult situation for James. I’ve been in that position myself before in my career and I know how tough it can be. He’s a very talented driver and a great guy, and I genuinely wish him all the best for whatever comes next.

“From my side, I’m absolutely buzzing to be coming back. Restart Racing feels like home to me and what we achieved together last year was something I’ll never forget. To win the team’s first outright BTCC race and then finish the year as Independent Champion was incredibly special.

“I’ve stayed really close to the team this season, working with everyone at the race weekends, so I’ve never really felt like I’ve been away from it. That makes coming back into the car feel very natural.

“I know the Hyundai, I know the team, and I know how hard everyone works behind the scenes. I’m coming back hungry, I want to enjoy it and, most importantly, I want to help the team finish the season as strongly as we possibly can.

“I can’t wait to get back behind the wheel at Donington.”

Lloyd returns to BTCC action at Donington Park GP (22/23 August) as the championship enters its final four events of the 2026 campaign.

title.rendered: Donington Park GP sets the stage for crucial weekend in 2026 campaign

excerpt.rendered: Now or never for the chasing pack as Sutton looks...

content.rendered:
Now or never for the chasing pack as Sutton looks to tighten title grip

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads to Donington Park this weekend (22/23 August), returning to the scene of the action-packed season opener, but this time around it’s on the iconic GP layout.

It was Adam Morgan, Ash Sutton and Tom Chilton who shared the victories last time out, with the middle man extending his championship advantage over Tom Ingram and Dan Cammish.

Now, the full Donington Park Grand Prix circuit awaits as the season begins its run towards the finale.

Familiar Ground, Different Stakes

Donington Park provides a familiar setting this weekend, but the 2.49-mile Grand Prix configuration offers a very different test to the National circuit which opened the campaign back in April.

The longer configuration returned to the BTCC calendar in 2023 after more than two decades away, adding the Melbourne section and its heavy braking zones to the familiar rush through Redgate, the Craner Curves and the Old Hairpin. Three years on, the GP circuit once again arrives at a crucial stage of the season, with just four events remaining in the 2026 title fight.

Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK - Ford) heads back to a layout where he won the opening race on its championship return three years ago and still holds the quickest Qualifying lap there of 1m33.154s. This time, however, the four-time champion arrives with an 81-point advantage and the opportunity to take another significant step towards a record fifth Drivers’ crown.

Tom Ingram (Team VERTU - Hyundai) is the driver with the clearest task of stopping him. The reigning champion sits second on 246 points and won around the Grand Prix circuit last season, while his 1m33.621s effort from the same weekend is the current race lap record. With opportunities to close Sutton down beginning to run out, Donington offers an important chance to turn proven pace at the venue into a championship gain.

Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK - Ford) has his own recent Donington success to draw upon, having taken victory on the GP layout in 2024. Just 13 points now separate the #27 from Ingram, meaning another strong weekend could move the Yorkshireman into second while simultaneously strengthening NAPA Racing UK’s hand at the top of the Teams’ standings. The trio at the top of the standings have each taken two triumphs around the GP layout, the joint-most of any driver on the 2026 grid.

The battle immediately behind the leading trio is even tighter. Ricky Collard (Team VERTU – Hyundai) arrives fourth on 180 points, with Charles Rainford (WSR – BMW) on 169 and Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) on 167. Doble also returns to Donington having taken victory on the National circuit at the opening event of 2026, although the extended GP configuration presents a very different challenge this weekend.

That fight extends further down the order too, with just 30 points covering fourth to tenth in the Drivers’ Championship. Doble also arrives at Donington at the head of the Independent Drivers’ standings, while Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) leads the way in the Jack Sears Trophy.

Saturday’s ‘Race to Pole’ means points are available before Sunday’s three contests even begin, adding another layer of importance to a weekend where recent Donington history, current form and an increasingly urgent title fight are set to collide.

TV, Timetables and Tickets

Complementing the tin top racing will be a sensational line-up of support series, as the Porsche Carrera Cup Great Britain, F4 British Championship certified by FIA MINI CHALLENGE Trophy and the Caterham Seven Championship UK complete the schedule of exciting races.

BTCC will be wowing the crowds both trackside and at home, with Saturday's 'Race to Pole' and the earlier qualifying session being streamed live via  ITV Sport's YouTube Channel from 1400, before ITV4's seven-and-a-half-hour race day broadcast gets underway at 1100 on Sunday.

Remember, continuing what started for the first time in the championship's history in 2025, the BTCC is being broadcast globally with every race being streamed live in 2026 via the BTCC YouTube Channel, whilst fans in North America can watch the action on the Racer Network. Look out for the races on Sunday starting at 1145, 1445 and 1730 (BST).

There's no place like being there, of course, and fans can purchase tickets in advance or on the gate throughout the weekend – visit here for more details.

title.rendered: Team VERTU takes victory from bruising Knockhill weekend

excerpt.rendered: Team VERTU ended a challenging weekend on a high at...

content.rendered:
Team VERTU ended a challenging weekend on a high at Knockhill with a third victory of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season.

The EXCELR8-run team headed for the Scottish circuit chasing a big haul of points to close the gap at the top of the standings, with Tom Ingram sitting second in the Drivers’ Championship and Team VERTU holding the same position in the Teams’ Championship.

Ingram would be drawn in the first qualifying group, and ended up sixth quickest having lost his fastest time to track limits, with Ricky Collard ending up as the lead Team VERTU driver on the grid for the Qualifying Race when he went fourth quickest in group two.

That left Collard eighth on the grid with Ingram in eleventh, with Tom Chilton lining up in 14th and Nic Hamilton starting from 20th.

The Race to Pole itself would be a relatively subdued affair for the team, with Collard making up a spot at the start but ultimately ending the race where he started after being overhauled by Mikey Doble on the run to the line.

Ingram managed to gain two places as he climbed to ninth spot, with Chilton also gaining two positions to twelfth and Hamilton taking the flag in 20th.

Vastly different conditions greeted the team for the opening race of the weekend on Sunday with rain falling, as all four drivers were able to stay out of trouble when the lights went out at the start - despite Ingram being slightly slow away from the line.

Collard managed to climb as high as fourth in the early stages before being overhauled for position, and he then allowed Ingram through to take fifth before the finish with the defending champion having worked his way onto the rear of his teammate.

Chilton had hoped to join them in the top ten but was found in the gravel at the chicane and dropped to the back of the field, although a safety car period allowed him to close up the rear of the pack before battling his way through to 17th place at the finish.

An off-track moment for Hamilton left him to make an unscheduled trip to the pits before he finished a lap down in 22nd.

Conditions had improved by the time race two came around, but it would prove to be a short-lived affair for Ingram when he was caught out by cars ahead jumping on the brakes to get through the chicane on lap one, with the resultant contact being sufficient to damage the radiator on his car and put him into retirement.

That left Collard to lead the team’s challenge with a typically feisty performance that saw him battle his way to fourth spot before finally finding a way ahead of race one winner Adam Morgan to bag his sixth podium of the campaign.

Chilton gained five spots to race his way into the points in twelfth, with Hamilton having looked on course to finish just outside the points until his car ground to a halt exiting the chicane on the penultimate lap following a late safety car period.

The reverse grid draw saw Chilton put onto pole for the final race of the weekend, and he made the most of experience - alongside the softer compound tyre - pay dividends as he led the way from start-to-finish to score his first victory of the campaign.

From tenth on the grid, Collard battled his way to ninth place on the medium tyre, with Ingram - complete with a new engine - also on the slower tyre but able to charge his way through from the back of the grid to take tenth and grab a few points back from Sutton in the championship race.

Running on the soft tyre, Hamilton ended the weekend with his most competitive performance to fall just shy of a points finish, taking the flag second amongst the Jack Sears Trophy runners.

Tom Chilton, #3 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “I’ve missed being on the top step of the podium so it’s nice to be taking a trophy home, particularly after it looked like it could be another of those weekends when I was facing the wrong way in the gravel in race one.

“When I got the reverse grid pole, I knew there was a real chance to go for the win, and I knew that I needed to make the most of the soft tyre in the early stages as I didn’t want to lose the opportunity. 

“I gave it everything and every lap was a qualifying lap to get the gap I needed, and even when the others closed in a bit later on, I’d been able to keep my TOCA Turbo Boost so I knew it was there if I needed it.

“Getting the win is great and is a good boost in confidence ahead of Donington Park GP, where I’ve gone well in recent years.”

Ricky Collard, #11 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “It’s been a good weekend for me across the board, and it helped that we had a stronger Saturday which meant I wasn’t trying to battle my way through the field as much on race day.

“To make it six podium finishes for the season and to move up to fourth in the championship standings is fantastic, and the team has done a great job this weekend to give me the tools that I needed.

“It’s great to see Tom Chilton get a win for the first time this season and it means everyone else in the team has been on the top step of the podium with Nic having his Jack Sears Trophy win. I’m the only one who hasn’t made it there yet, so I need to make sure I put that right!”

Nicolas Hamilton, #28 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “I turned up this weekend feeling really positive, but it’s been a difficult weekend with the changeable weather conditions. Free practice was a really positive start as I was half a second quicker than last season, and then I was quicker again in qualifying before the weather started to have an impact.

“When the rain arrived, I was on the back foot a bit because I don’t have the experience of the car in those conditions to really get the most from it. There are a lot of things that we need to think about with my car with the servo brake system and what bias we run, and in race one in particular when it was properly wet, I just didn’t feel comfortable.

“We were quicker in the second race and I felt more at home before the alternator failed right at the end, and the team did a great job to make some changes for race three where we tried something new that worked. I started from 19th and came through to 16th despite losing places at the start, which was a solid way to end things.

“Obviously it would have been nice to score a point, but it was still a good way to end a challenging weekend.”

Tom Ingram, #80 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “As a team, it’s good to have come away from Knockhill with some trophies but it’s been a bruising weekend for me personally, and one where the only luck I had was bad luck. 

“Had it not been for track limits, we’d have been up on the third row of the grid for the qualifying race rather than stuck in the pack where it was hard to try and make progress with the amount of boost that we had.

“We had an issue with the car in race one that meant I didn’t get the best of starts but we still managed to climb to fifth, and then in race two going into the chicane, the guys in front concertinaed up and there was nowhere to go. It didn’t look like the biggest of hits but it did a lot of damage, and that was game over.

“Because of the issues in the first two races, we changed the engine for race three, and that is probably the high point of the weekend for me because the team did an outrageous job to get that sorted in 45 minutes - it was an unbelievable effort.

“To come from the back of the grid to finish in the top ten was good in terms of making up places, but obviously we’ve not scored the points we were hoping for this weekend which is disappointing. However, we’ll keep pushing hard and will come out fighting when we get to Donington Park in a few weeks time.”

title.rendered: Restart Racing battle through Knockhill race day

excerpt.rendered: Restart Racing battled through a thrilling day of mixed conditions...

content.rendered:
Restart Racing battled through a thrilling day of mixed conditions at Knockhill in the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship, with Chris Smiley (#22) and James Dorlin (#132) scoring a double points finish.

The team entered Sunday encouraged by its strongest qualifying performance of the campaign. Smiley secured fourth in Saturday’s Race to Pole, while Dorlin would come 15th after contact whilst running in the top eight.

A heavy downpour shortly before the opening bout of race day left the circuit in treacherous conditions with limited visibility. The whole grid, including both Restart Racing Hyundai i30 N cars, started on wet tyres.

Smiley started from fourth but immediately dropped to fifth after Charles Rainford (WSR) passed him at Duffus Dip on the opening lap. Dorlin’s start differed, gaining two positions to move into 13th.

The difficult conditions soon began to affect the #22, who was struggling with a misted windscreen, causing visibility issues. After losing ground, Dorlin moved ahead of Smiley at Taylor’s Hairpin on lap seven, placing the duo 13th and 14th.

Smiley’s race became even more challenging when contact with Árón Taylor-Smith (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport) saw him off the circuit at McIntyre’s. The Irishman recovered to 19th, while Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing) passed Dorlin as the pair continued to battle in the midfield.

The Yorkshireman initially crossed the line in 16th, directly ahead of Smiley in 17th. Both drivers were subsequently promoted one position following a penalty for NAPA Racing UK’s Dan Cammish, pushing the pair up one spot each.

With the circuit dry for the middle race of the day, both drivers switched to the soft tyre. Both drivers gained a position during a frenetic opening lap. The Safety Car was deployed to allow the stricken car of Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) to be recovered.

Racing resumed on lap five, with Smiley making strong progress through the order as he recovered from an early setback.

A string of overtakes lifted the Restart Racing driver into the top ten before he passed Cammish for ninth. His charge was brought to a premature end on lap 22, however, when damage sustained earlier in the race led to a front upright failure and sent him into the gravel at Duffus Dip.

The incident resulted in the team’s first retirement of the season and triggered a second Safety Car period. Dorlin also made ground following the restart, eventually taking the chequered flag in 14th.

Both cars ran the medium tyre for the final race, with Dorlin starting 14th and Smiley lining up 20th following his earlier retirement.

The #22 made immediate progress through the field, while Dorlin was shuffled back following contact with Daryl De Leon (WSR) in the opening laps.

The pair later found themselves in a close battle with championship leader Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK), with both Restart Racing cars briefly moving ahead during a lively scrap for the points-paying positions.

Smiley and Dorlin continued to run closely together through the closing stages but were unable to make further progress, eventually taking the chequered flag in 14th and 15th respectively to secure a double-points finish for the team.

Chris Smiley, #22 Restart Racing, said: “That’s Knockhill finished for another year. It promised to be one of our best weekends after the pace we showed in Qualifying and the Race to Pole.

“I started race one from fourth and unfortunately had an issue with my heated windscreen. I couldn’t see where I was going, so we fell back and eventually finished 16th.

“We made great progress in race two and climbed from 16th to ninth. I had a slight lock-up on some water on the inside at Taylor’s Hairpin and made unintentional contact with another car. That damaged the front upright, which then failed as I went into Duffus Dip and caused our first DNF of the season.

“We started race three from 20th on the medium tyre, and recovered to finish 14th. We’re going home feeling as though we’ve let a weekend get away from us because it could have delivered much more.”

James Dorlin, #132 Restart Racing, said: “Knockhill is done, and it had been a really, really tough weekend. We had the pace to be right at the front, but we weren’t in the right place at the right time and kept getting pushed around.

“In race three, we were moving forward during the opening laps and the car felt good. I was pushed wide on lap two; it compromised our race because, although we recovered several positions, we had lost too much ground through that initial contact.

“That’s touring car racing, unfortunately, especially around a circuit like Knockhill. It’s one to put behind us, and I’m really looking forward to Donington Park and seeing what we can achieve there.”

title.rendered: Tin Top Tuesday powered by Power Maxed - Knockhill

excerpt.rendered: The BTCC headed north to Knockhill for the sixth event...

content.rendered:
The BTCC headed north to Knockhill for the sixth event of the year, showcasing three spectacular races plus another thrilling Qualifying race in Scotland. The Fife rollercoaster delivered a frenetic, record-setting start to the second half of the season.

As the 2026 season continues to take full flight, take a listen to the sixth instalment of Tin Top Tuesday powered by Power Maxed, which was aired earlier this week (Tuesday, 11 August).

The podcast opened with none other than Adam Morgan (Cataclean Plato Racing), as the Mercedes A35 Saloon driver took the new outfit's maiden BTCC triumph. The Lancastrian also headed the team's first one-two on Sunday after taking the fastest time in Qualifying and pole position after finishing first in the 'Race to Pole' a day prior.

Oly Collins (Team Manager, NAPA Racing UK) was the next guest on the show, speaking on the Alliance Racing-run squad not taking time off over the traditional summer break. Collins also spoke on Ash Sutton's impressive seven wins so far this campaign, commending the crew behind the four-time champ for their efforts to support the championship leader.

Alan Hyde also caught up with Tom Chilton (Team VERTU) after the Hyundai i30 N racer took his 19th career BTCC victory, with the most recent race going the way of the #3. Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing) was next on the show after a career-high weekend that saw the Scot's best single-race finish whilst also taking his highest-scoring weekend in the BTCC. Patterson's stablemate Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) also joined the show after a rollercoaster weekend left the Scot with a less-than-ideal result at his home venue.

Moffat and the rest of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship grid head to Donington Park (22/23 August) for the second visit to the circuit this year, this time around the GP layout for the seventh race weekend of the campaign.

Listen to the full show below...

title.rendered: WSR in top six on challenging Knockhill weekend

excerpt.rendered: WSR concluded a challenging mixed-weather Kwik Fit British Touring Car...

content.rendered:
WSR concluded a challenging mixed-weather Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship trip across the border to Knockhill, Scotland, with a trio of top-six finishes.

Drivers Charles Rainford and Daryl De Leon showed fighting spirit all the way aboard their BMW 330i M Sport cars in the final race of the weekend, securing more valuable points in the Independents Trophy with fifth and sixth places respectively.

Lewis Gilbert’s first BTCC outing on home soil was another learning curve for the 22-year-old, but the Ayrshire driver ended the weekend with an 18th-place finish after two retirements earlier in the day.

Rainford, sporting a special one-off livery for Knockhill, started the wet opener from sixth place but had to pit to remove a loose rear bumper after receiving a black flag with an orange disc at two-thirds distance, dropping him down the order.

A further spin after contact limited him to 21st at the flag, but a sensational charge through the field on the soft-compound tyre in race two brought the Horsham racer to sixth once again.

Another strong drive in the third race showcased the BMW's speed as Rainford secured a well-earned top-five result and his best of the day.

In race three, De Leon was also on the move after a frustrating second race, leaping 11 places to finish just behind Rainford in sixth.

The 20-year-old Anglo-Filipino, the reigning Jack Sears Trophy champion, had been in the mix for a solid top-six result in the opening bout before contact sent him through the gravel trap, relegating him to 11th.

Race two was a similar story as contact with Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK) saw De Leon off at Clark Corner, eventually resulting in a 17th-place result.

Competing with the support of the local crowd, Gilbert impressed in Saturday’s Qualifying Race, but did not finish Sunday’s opener after contact under braking for Clark.

Another incident in the second race of the day curtailed his chances of a points-scoring result. A learning weekend concluded with a deserved finish, after an early spin.

Charles Rainford: “We had amazing pace in Race One, but unfortunately, I had contact at the rear, which caused me to get a mechanical black flag, and then I had more contact after the Safety Car, which wasn’t ideal. I used that frustration in Race Two to get from 21st to sixth, and then I did the maximum I could in Race Three with a bit of damage. Overall, it had been a good day, with some nice points. We’ve been really good at Donington earlier in the year so hopefully we can repeat that pace next time out.”

Daryl De Leon: “It was a tough race day at Knockhill. We had some good pace in Race One, but with contact we lost three or four places. Then, in Race Two, I ended up in the barriers. Thankfully I managed to continue and finish 17th. In the final race, I was on the medium tyre and worked my way up to sixth from 17th with a lot of overtakes. Although the racing hadn’t gone our way this time, the atmosphere in Scotland has been amazing.”

Lewis Gilbert: “This weekend has been a good learning curve for me in the BTCC, especially in front of my home crowd - which was incredible. I was really happy with my pace in the final race, which was quite similar to the race winner on the same tyres. The first two races were a bit disappointing due to the issues, but we made a good step towards the end of the day, and I am already looking forward to getting back out there at Donington.”

Dick Bennetts, Team Principal: “It has been a good and bad day, but we can take the positives with all three cars reaching the finish in more or less one piece. Daryl had a strong final race, moving from 17th to sixth, and Charles was very impressive in the second race. For Lewis, it’s been another learning curve, and his pace was matching the leaders in Race Three, which is a big positive. The speed he has shown in the car with his limited experience has been incredible. Roll on Donington…”

title.rendered: Breakthrough weekend for Cataclean Plato Racing

excerpt.rendered: Rounds 16, 17 and 18 of the 2026 Kwik Fit...

content.rendered:
Rounds 16, 17 and 18 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship produced three different winners from three different teams, but it was Cataclean Plato Racing’s breakthrough weekend that stole the headlines at Knockhill.

Adam Morgan set the pace in qualifying, won Saturday afternoon’s ‘Race to Pole’ contest and then converted that form into victory in Sunday’s opening race.

The celebrations were further enhanced for the Mercedes squad as Dan Rowbottom completed a historic Cataclean Plato Racing one-two, with Team Principal and tin-top legend Jason Plato watching on.

The team’s strong form continued, while the remaining victories went to championship leader Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) and Tom Chilton (Team VERTU – Hyundai), as the BTCC title battle continued to take shape amid mixed conditions in Scotland.

Sutton is closing in on a potential record-breaking fifth overall drivers’ title and left the tight, twisty circuit with a firm grip on proceedings, while second-placed Tom Ingram lost ground to Dan Cammish.

Four-time champ Sutton holds an 81-point lead at the top of the order, whilst Cammish has closed to within 13 points of second placed Ingram.

Alliance Racing/Ford and its NAPA Racing UK outfit retain a commanding advantage at the top of both the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ and Teams’ standings, while Mikey Doble and LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing remain in control of the Independents’ honours.

Dexter Patterson also enjoyed a standout weekend, pulling clear of James Dorlin in the race for the Jack Sears Trophy.

The BTCC returns to action in two weeks’ time, on 22/23 August, at Donington Park.

Morgan survives the showers for first Cataclean Plato Racing victory

Lancastrian Morgan claimed victory in the Knockhill opener, securing Cataclean Plato Racing’s first win while leading home a one-two finish ahead of teammate Rowbottom.

The success is testament to the hard work put in by the rookie squad, and particularly the progress made with the Mercedes A35 Saloons since the mid-summer break.

Morgan had to contend with wet conditions and a late race safety car intervention, but the multiple race winner was always in control of the contest, as Rowbottom played rear gunner in the closing laps.

Rowbottom had earlier relinquished Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport's Gordon Shedden of second with an impressive move, whilst the Scotsman then had to turn his attentions to his rear mirrors.

Incredibly, there were nine Drivers' titles between the racers battling for third at the finish, as Toyota man Shedden saw off the challenges from the title chasing duo of Sutton (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) and Ingram (Team VERTU – Hyundai).

Sutton had got the better of Ingram in the earlier running with the former charging up through the order from 11th on the grid.

A series of stellar moves in extreme conditions looked set to secure another rostrum finish for the #116 Ford Focus Titanium, but as Ingram’s #80 Hyundai i30N gradually closed in, Sutton’s focus shifted to keeping his old adversary behind.

Seventh heaven for Sutton

NAPA Racing UK's Sutton surged to victory in Round 17, to take his seventh race win of the campaign and extend his advantage at the top of the standings.

Starting from fourth on the grid, Sutton’s Ford made light work of Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport – Toyota) and Morgan (Cataclean Plato Racing – Mercedes) ahead of him before he set about attacking Rowbottom (Cataclean Plato Racing – Mercedes) for the lead.

There was disappointment behind for Sutton’s main title rival, Team VERTU’s Ingram, who was already nursing a power issue off the line before being forced into retirement after contact. As the field concertinaed ahead, the #80 Hyundai ran into the rear of Shedden’s Toyota on the first run to the chicane and was immediately forced to pit with radiator damage.

Rowbottom performed extremely well in the #32 Mercedes A35 Saloon out front, particularly considering the lack of boost available while also running the harder Goodyear tyre compound.

There was little Rowbottom could do to stop his former teammate however, as Sutton's #116 Ford Focus Titanium sliced down the inside at the final hairpin.

Two safety car periods interrupted proceedings with the second delay only allowing for a final one-lap shootout at the finish.

Sutton cruised home while Rowbottom fended off the Hyundai of Team VERTU's Ricky Collard, who again continued his impressive BTCC season in style.

Chilton charges to first victory of 2026

Team VERTU's Chilton took his 19th career BTCC triumph and the third of his career at Knockhill.

The experienced tin top star has endured a mixed 2026 campaign so far with a solitary podium at Snetterton being a high point, but those misfortunes are now a thing of the past as the #3 Hyundai driver dominated the finale in Scotland.

If Chilton was pleased with his pillar-to-post triumph then Morgan was overjoyed with his weekend's work as he ended the day with a second place, following on from his 'Race to Pole' win, race one victory and another top five finish – comfortably the Cataclean Plato Racing driver's best weekend of the season so far.

It’s a huge credit to the team, the sponsors and everybody involved – a huge thank you.”

title.rendered: Sutton seals seventh success in Scotland

excerpt.rendered: NAPA Racing UK's Ash Sutton surged to victory in Round...

content.rendered:
NAPA Racing UK's Ash Sutton surged to victory in Round 17 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Knockhill, to take his seventh race win of the campaign and extend his advantage at the top of the standings.

Starting from fourth on the grid, Sutton made light work of Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport) and Adam Morgan (Cataclean Plato Racing) ahead of him before he set about attacking Daniel Rowbottom (Cataclean Plato Racing) for the lead.

There was disappointment behind for Sutton's main title rival – Team VERTU's Tom Ingram – already nursing a power problem off the line before he was soon forced into retirement following contact. As the action concertinaed ahead of him, the #80 Hyundai went into the back of Shedden's Toyota on the run to the chicane for the first time, and immediately had to pit with radiator damage.

Local favourite Aiden Moffat was another early casualty when his LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing Audi was caught up in a separate incident.

Rowbottom performed extremely well in the #32 Mercedes A35 Saloon out front, particularly considering the lack of boost available while also running the harder Goodyear tyre compound.

There was little Rowbottom could do to stop his former teammate however, as Sutton's #116 Ford Focus Titanium sliced down the inside at the final hairpin.

Two safety car periods interrupted proceedings with the second delay only allowing for a final one-lap shootout at the finish.

Sutton's cruised home while Rowbottom fended off Team VERTU's Ricky Collard, who again continues his standout BTCC season in style.

Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) and Charles Rainford (WSR) starred in fourth and sixth respectively with the latter bursting through from 21st on the grid following his difficult opening race this morning.

Morgan ensured that it was another double celebration for Cataclean Plato Racing with a top five finish, again running on the harder tyre and with minimal boost.

Three-time champion Shedden hung on to seventh ahead of fellow countryman Dexter Patterson in the #17 Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing Audi.

A trio of NAPA Racing UK cars followed in the order with Dan Cammish, Sam Osborne and Lewis Selby finishing in ninth, tenth and eleventh respectively.
